summary: Made the extension's scaffolded output agree with the tutorial Session 1 rewrote, changing template content and doc text only - no scaffolder logic, no new commands, no Work Explorer changes. CODEOWNERS.template dropped the retired three-person cast (greeter/clock/integration, @priya-gh/@sam-gh/@alex-gh) for the tutorial's two modules, with its worked example reduced to exactly the two rule lines the tutorial tells the reader to uncomment, in the same leading-slash form the tutorial prints; the plan-folder ownership rules, the three-paragraph integration-touches narration, and the commented conflict-magnet rule pair all went (41 -> 27 lines). monorepo-ci.yml.template was cut 84 -> 43 lines: the active job is renamed all-modules -> test and its push-only `if:` gate removed, so it runs on every pull request as well as every push to main, and the ~45-line commented paths-filter block became a four-line pointer. Both changes exist because the tutorial has the reader require a status check literally named `test`, and on GitHub the required-check name IS the job name - a scaffolded mismatch would have had readers renaming a job GitHub had already been told to require. getting-started.md.template now points at docs/tutorials/hello-world.md and drops the review-prompt URL, whose target Session 1 deleted; its 'rename Default' advice now says what Dabbler: Rename Module does and does not carry, using Session 1's empirical finding, because the old wording tacitly contradicted the tutorial's deliberate use of New Module + Delete Module. Cold-start goldens regenerated through the sanctioned UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 path and dist/ rebuilt, so template, golden, and shipped copy are byte-identical - asserted, not assumed, by the proof's check C. The spec's demand that green-on-empty be proven rather than asserted was met by execution: a structure pass establishes the active job's only repo-contributed failure surface is its run block, that exact block then runs under bash -e in a fresh empty git repo (exit 0, writes nothing), and parity is checked across all three templates and both tiers - 29/29 PASS, with the three things it cannot prove locally named rather than glossed. Extension bumped 0.45.0 -> 0.46.0 with a template-bundle-only CHANGELOG section; dabbler-ai-router deliberately NOT bumped (this session touched zero files under ai_router/), said explicitly rather than left implicit. Nothing was published and no tag was pushed. Suite green across all three layers on the shipped tree: 3060 passed / 6 skipped (pytest), 1767 passing (extension unit), 28 passed (Playwright, run because the cold-start fixture tree changed - L-064-12). Verification: round 1 discovery (fan-out 2/2) VERIFIED with three nits, round 2 discovery (fan-out 2/2) VERIFIED with five - zero blocking findings in either, so the loop closed at the two-pass bound with no remediation cycle ever opened. All eight nits were fixed anyway because each was a factual error in this session's own prose or a one-line wording repair; round 2 is the one that earned its cost, catching three inaccuracies round 1 had passed, two of them inside the proof artifact whose whole purpose is to stop this session asserting what it has not established (a hand-typed 31/31 tally against 27 printed checks, and a wrong rationale excusing one file from byte comparison). The tally is now machine-computed from the counter that prints the checks, so it cannot drift again.

reason.specifics: The routed step-3.5 analysis (gemini-2.5-pro, anthropic excluded) recommends codex/openai/gpt-5.6 for Session 3: authoring six OBS scene scripts plus the S4 UAT checklist is precision-structured prose work where a different model family adds cognitive diversity. This is the SECOND consecutive recommendation to switch off Anthropic for this set - Session 1's advisor said the same for Session 2, and the operator invoked Claude anyway. Recorded, not disputed: the counter-argument is genuinely thinner here than it was for S2, because S3 authors new files against a finished tutorial rather than keeping two surfaces consistent, and S3 is the last chance for independent eyes on the teaching sequence before the operator spends ~2 hours walking it in S4. The pick remains the operator's at invocation; continuing on claude-opus-5 is defensible but buys less than it did this session.

residual_findings: TUTORIAL-SIDE, NOT FIXED HERE (Session 2 does not own docs/tutorials/hello-world.md; the spec assigns it to S1 and lets S3 touch it only if scripting exposes a gap). Part 4 step 6 instructs the reader to 'adapt the scaffolded file down to exactly one active job' and to 'delete any `if: github.event_name == 'push' ...` line'. After this re-cut there is exactly one active job and no `if:` line, so both clauses are now no-ops. The wording is conditional ('any'), so it is stale rather than false, and the tutorial's minimal-edit promise is better satisfied than before - but S3 should trim it when it scripts scene 4.

TUTORIAL-SIDE, NOT FIXED HERE. The same step says 'replace the placeholder `run:` block with a real test command', while its finished YAML also adds an actions/setup-python@v5 step and a `python -m pip install pytest` step that the language-agnostic template cannot carry. The tutorial prints the complete target file, so a reader can match it - but the prose undersells the edit by two steps. S3 should reconcile the sentence with the snippet.

PRE-EXISTING, OUT OF SCOPE. tools/dabbler-ai-orchestration/package-lock.json still reads 0.41.0 while package.json is now 0.46.0. This drift predates this session by at least four releases (0.42.0-0.45.0 all shipped with it stale) and was deliberately left alone rather than folded into a template-content session.
declined_recommendations: The routed CI-template analysis recommended a FAIL-CLOSED placeholder: a run block exiting 0 when no modules exist and 1 once any appear, so a consumer cannot end up with a green required check that tests nothing. Declined, and the reasoning is on the record because it is a judgment call rather than a fact. It hardcodes `services/` as the module location into a template that is deliberately layout- and language-agnostic (codeRoots can be any path), so it would fail-open anyway on any repo not using that convention; it would go red on a fresh repo holding a services/ directory for unrelated reasons, which is exactly the harmless-as-scaffolded property the spec makes binding; and it is arguably a behavior change, which this set's non-goals forbid. Adopted instead: a ::warning:: annotation on every run - zero branching, zero layout assumptions - so the placeholder is visible rather than silent. Round 1's verifier correctly noted that visible is not unmissable, and the CHANGELOG now says so in as many words rather than overclaiming. The residual hazard is real and named, not closed.

The same analysis proposed proving green-on-empty with `act` (a Docker-backed local GitHub Actions runner). Not installed on this machine, and installing one was judged disproportionate for a three-echo run block. The substitute keeps the standard - run the thing - at the level actually reachable: a structure pass that establishes the run block is the ONLY repo-contributed failure surface, which is what makes executing just that block sufficient. What remains unproven locally is named in the artifact rather than papered over.
